To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the response rate of uniformly accelerated sources in the presence of walls parallel to their direction of motion can be calculated by considering the thermal field of an accelerated observer in Minkowski space, provided that the same boundary conditions imposed to the field in Minkowskian vacuum are also imposed to the thermal field.
the response rate of an accelerated point source is not affected by boundaries and the same response rate can be obtained from the point of an accelerated detector.

the boundary conditions imposed to the scalar field are crucial for the determination of the response rate of an accelerated source, that in a waveguide the response rate is strongly inhibited, that in a tube of realistic width the response rate is practically zero for any particle acceleration, and that the response rate is the same in the inertial and in the coacceleration frames.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the response rate of an accelerated point source interacting through a massless real field in the presence of a boundary.
the problem of a uniformly accelerated particle in a cavity.
the study of the influence of boundaries on the response rate of uniformly accelerated sources, and we show that this rate is strongly inhibited for a wide range of physical parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the boundary conditions on the walls of the waveguide are responsible for the inhibition of the rate of the response of the source, and not the existence of the thermal bath.
the response rate in a uniformly accelerated frame is a consequence of the thermal nature of the vacuum and the boundary conditions on the surface, but not of the acceleration itself.
the response rate is not a frame-dependent quantity, and it is the same in the uniformly accelerated frame and in the coaccelerate frame, as expected from the Unruh effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the response rate is a function of the geometry of the system and of the boundary conditions.
the presence of the boundary conditions in the coacceleration frame is enough to reproduce the same results as those obtained in the inertial frame.
the response rate in the coacceleration frame is the response rate in Minkowski space with the thermal bath, but with the boundary conditions of the original frame.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of walls, the response rate is sensitive to the boundary conditions imposed on the field, which is not the case for the Fulling-Davis-Unruh effect.

the response rate of the uniformly accelerated source can be obtained from the thermal field response rate in a coaccelerated reference frame, and this fact is independent of the boundary conditions imposed to the thermal bath.
the response rate of the accelerated point source is a frame dependent quantity.
